The scan shows an unprinted leaf. Faint browning and foxing, a dark band along the top edge and a darker strip along the left edge are paper discolouration or the edge of the neighbouring page, not print. No running head, page number, catchword, signature or marginal notes are visible.
Blank leaf. Only stains and paper discolouration are visible. The faint mark in the lower right corner is not printed text and is not transcribed.

The scan shows a blank leaf of aged, yellowed paper with only foxing, stains and faint show-through. There is no printed text, heading, page number, running head or catchword. The only mark is a faint printed or stamped line in the lower right corner, which is a digitiser or library mark and is left out. No transcription is possible.

Blank leaf. Only foxing and staining are visible; no printed words, numbers, headings, running heads, catchwords or signatures can be found. A faint mark in the lower right corner is a scanner or cover artefact, not printed text. The edge of the adjacent page and the scanning background are excluded.

Blank page with stains, foxing, tears and creases. Two dark blue rectangles (upper right and lower centre) look like scanner or digitiser covers or stamps, so they are left out. No printed text, page number, running head, catchword or signature is visible.

The scan shows only a blank, yellowed page surface with stains, foxing and show-through. A pink fingertip intrudes at the lower left, and a binding edge or neighbouring page is visible at the right. No printed text, running head, page number, catchword or signature is visible, so nothing has been transcribed.
